title: Score adjacent-page similarity and its drops at section and Currier transitions against a generator whose tables change at those boundaries
statement: Work on K-003-open-1, public training pages only (192 pages, 189 consecutive pairs with at least 40 certain words each, 43 of them crossing a section or Currier-language boundary). Similarity here is the cosine of raw word-count vectors of consecutive pages, not the paper's latent semantic analysis, so this is a simpler stand-in under one preprocessing for every text; synthetic texts have the manuscript's page and line shapes word for word. Manuscript: median 0.344 (5th to 95th percentile 0.106 to 0.648), against 0.197 for pages in shuffled order; of the 9 lowest scores (5%), 5 fall on transitions, which make up 23% of pairs; median at transitions 0.170. Pinned self-citation generator: median 0.007, shuffled 0.007, so it has almost no page-to-page similarity at all and no usable low tail. Glyph chain with one table for the whole text (the procedure that landed on F-002, F-004, F-005): median 0.313 but 0.326 shuffled, and none of its 9 lowest scores on transitions, so it has no neighbourhood effect. The same glyph chain with a separate table fitted for each Currier language and section, the change being fixed in advance by the page's label: median 0.346 (0.135 to 0.757), 0.256 shuffled, 5 of its 9 lowest scores on transitions, median at transitions 0.250. So on public pages the answer is yes in outline: a meaning-free procedure whose tables change at prespecified boundaries reproduces the level of adjacent-page similarity and where the low scores fall; it is less sharp than the manuscript at transitions (0.250 against 0.170) and its upper tail is heavier. Limits: 9 low scores is a small count; the generator is fitted on the same public pages it is compared on; nothing here is scored on hidden pages. Proposed step: add an adjacent-page similarity statistic to the measurement language (reviewed code), register (a) adjacent above shuffled-order similarity and (b) the share of lowest-5% scores at transitions as facts, then attack both with the per-section glyph chain using the line-keeping cut.
check: fact.json for the two statistics once the statistic exists, scored on hidden pages and on Takahashi; then attack.json with cut lines from a glyph chain fitted per Currier language and section on public pages only.
